text:
alex: FYI: customer saw duplicate billing when a model-swap and reconnect overlapped with our prefetch heartbeat. putting quick trace here.

maria: ouch. which pipeline? streaming generate + background prefetch?

alex: yes. /v1/generate, model swap happened mid-stream (canary). prefetch sent provisional, then swap triggered truncate+resume, later provisional got confirmed -> double count.

chen: can you paste the minimal trace?

alex: snippet:
```
[2025-01-14T09:12:01Z] stream:start session=sess42 model=v1
[2025-01-14T09:12:03Z] prefetch:heartbeat provisional=pp-42 window=[200:260]
[2025-01-14T09:12:04Z] model-swap:commit model=v2
[2025-01-14T09:12:04Z] stream:truncate suffix=60
[2025-01-14T09:12:05Z] client:resume session=sess42 resume=true
[2025-01-14T09:12:06Z] ledger:confirm provisional=pp-42 -> confirmed
```

maria: So confirm happens after truncate+resume. We need a way to ensure confirms can't retroactively claim trimmed tokens.

jon: Two obvious fixes: attach session-epoch to provisional and require confirm to match current session-epoch; or tombstone provisional on truncate.

chen: Epoch attach sounds cleaner: every resume increments epoch nonce. Confirm checks epoch == provisional. No tombstone GC needed.

alex: But prefetch runs in background and may create provisionals before client gets resume handshake. If epoch changes, confirm will fail and we need to surface reason. That's fine but might create churn in metrics.

maria: What's the failure mode? Confirm rejected -> provisional left dangling until compactor removes it. That still needs GC. Tombstone is explicit but adds writes.

jon: Hybrid: session-epoch for fast rejection + tombstone-on-truncate for an explicit marker in edge cases. Tombstone only for truncates from model-swap or manual trims (low frequency).

chen: That minimizes writes while giving safety. Confirm path: if epoch mismatch -> reject and emit metric; if tombstone present -> reject and increment tombstone_rejects.

alex: Also add a reconciler job that scans provisional ledger rows older than X and reconciles to ensure no drift. It can also emit delta to billing reconcile topic.

sre-bot: alert: canary billing anomaly rate increased x3 last 6h (tag: provisional_rejects)

maria: ops ask: add console panels: provisional rejections by reason (epoch_mismatch, tombstone) and per-route heatmap. We need to correlate with rollouts (model swap ids).

jon: For canary testing: add artificial 200ms confirm-delay injection to surface races; add unit tests where confirm arrives before/after truncate; assert ledger net delta == one charge.

chen: We should also change confirm RPC to be idempotent: include provisional id + expected offset range and hash of prefix so double-confirms with overlapping ranges can be detected and only one wins.

alex: Good point. Prefix-hash check avoids subtle off-by-one overlaps. We'll add a conditional write: commit only if current_range overlaps and no prior commit for that token-range.

maria: Migration plan? We'll need to backfill session-epochs for live sessions or treat missing epoch as permissive for a short migration window and rely on tombstones.

jon: Migration: default missing epoch -> confirm allowed but emit migration_warning metric. After rollout window, require epoch for confirms and reject missing ones.

alex: I'll put together a PR with: epoch field on provisional, tombstone write on truncate (only non-zero suffix events), confirm guards (epoch check + tombstone check + prefix-hash), compactor job, reconciler job, metrics, and console widgets.

chen: tests + canary rule + docs in console rollouts page. Also ping CS so they know about provisional rejections during migration.

maria: sounds good. assign reviewers: @jon @chen. thanks.

alex: will open PR today and tag reviewers. monitoring panics if rate > 0.5% in canary.

jon: ack. :thumbsup:
